data.name: TabSde
data.comment: CCP's Static Data Export; usually left as SDE.

data.name: TabPolling
data.comment: How often the app asks ESI for new data.

data.name: LanguageSystemDefault
data.comment: {0} is the language the system setting comes to, in that language's own name.

data.name: LanguagePreview
data.comment: {0} is a language's own name. Preview: not fully translated yet.

data.name: LanguagePreviewNote
data.value: Preview: parts of the app are not translated yet and show in English.

data.name: LanguageRestartNote
data.value: The new language is used from the next start.

data.name: AppearanceNote
data.value: Theme and scale apply at once to every window and dialog, and the language from the next start. All three are remembered for this client only — a second client on the same database keeps its own. The scale is also on the status bar, at the right end, for a quick change.

data.name: EveTimeLinkNote
data.value: Clicking the EVE clock in the title bar opens this site. Pick one of the suggestions or choose Custom URL and enter your own.

data.name: CustomUrlOption
data.comment: An entry in the list of sites; must match the name used in EveTimeLinkNote.

data.name: ServerStatusNote
data.value: Clicking the Tranquility indicator beside the clock opens CCP's official service status page. Not configurable — no other site carries the same information.
data.comment: Tranquility is the name of EVE's main server.

data.name: ABrowserTabWillNote
data.value: A browser tab will open for you to log in and authorize access. Review the scopes below and uncheck any you do not want to grant. These choices apply to this authentication only.

data.name: RemovingScopesWillDisableNote
data.value: Removing scopes will disable related features in this application. They can be re-granted at any time by running Update.

data.name: ANewerEveStaticNote
data.value: A newer Eve static data build is available.

data.name: BlueprintsReprocessingCompressionAndNote
data.value: Blueprints, reprocessing, compression, and repackaged volumes updated shortly after each TQ patch — often ahead of the official SDE.

data.name: TipPersonalCorpsCountToward
data.value: Personal corps count toward your individual net worth. Alliance or employer corps are treated as separate entities.

data.name: WhichCharactersMayBeNote
data.value: Which characters may be given industry jobs, and on what. Every authorised character is listed automatically with all three activities on — clear the ones a character should not be given, which is how an alt is taken out of consideration. Jobs go to the least capable character who can run them, keeping the high-skill alts free for the work only they can do. Clear Skill queue for a character whose queue is empty on purpose, and it raises no skill queue alerts.

data.name: TipCharacterSkillQueueShould
data.value: Character skill queue should be kept running. Clear it for an alt whose queue is deliberately empty, and neither the Overview alerts nor the worklist will report it.

data.name: TipDownloadAndImportThe
data.value: Download and import the latest Eve static data. Can be run even if already up to date.

data.name: BlueprintsReprocessingCompressionAndNote2
data.value: Blueprints, reprocessing, compression, and repackaged volumes — updated shortly after each TQ patch, often ahead of the official SDE.

data.name: TipDownloadBlueprintReprocessingCompression
data.value: Download blueprint, reprocessing, compression, and repackaged-volume data from sde.hoboleaks.space.

data.name: FuzzworkFetchesPreComputedNote
data.value: Fuzzwork: fetches pre-computed percentile prices from fuzzwork.co.uk. Fast, requires no auth, and stores very little data locally (one price row per item). Does not store individual orders — the Market Orders tab in the Item Browser requires ESI Region or ESI Structure.

data.name: EsiRegionFetchesAllNote
data.value: ESI Region: fetches all public orders for an entire region from ESI. Use this for NPC trade hubs (e.g. Jita → The Forge). Note: orders posted inside player-owned structures are not included — only regional buy orders placed in structures appear.

data.name: PlayerStructureFetchesAllNote
data.value: Player Structure: fetches all orders within a specific player-owned structure (citadel, engineering complex, etc.). Requires an auth character with docking access. Use this for null-sec staging keeps and other private markets.

data.name: HintEGJita44
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: HintStationOrStructureId
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: SearchForAStationNote
data.value: Search for a station or structure by name. Results populate the Location ID above.

data.name: HintStationOrStructureName
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: RestrictPricesToANote
data.value: Restrict prices to a single station (e.g. Jita 4-4). Refresh the source first to populate the list.

data.name: RemovesAnomaliesCausedByNote
data.value: Removes anomalies caused by small-volume orders at the extremes of the order book. Sell = Nth-percentile cheapest; Buy = (100-N)th-percentile highest.

data.name: AppliedWhenTheMarketNote
data.value: Applied when the market has no sell orders for an item. Price = build cost × (1 + markup%). If no buy orders, buy defaults to sell.

data.name: AppliesToEsiRegionNote
data.value: Applies to ESI region / structure markets only. Orders visible in the market UI but excluded from buy price calculation.

data.name: ABackgroundJobRefreshesNote
data.value: A background job refreshes 30-day market history for every traded item in these regions, once per 24 hours per item, so the opportunity tools and item details read it straight from the DB. It paces itself against ESI's error limit, so it will never push the app over. Large regions (e.g. The Forge) fill in gradually across sessions.

data.name: HintSelectARegionToAdd
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: TipWatchLivePerNote
data.value: Tip: watch live per-region sweep progress (refreshed vs queued, and whether it's running) on the Background Processes → Price History tab.

data.name: RecalculateStoredBuildCostsNote
data.value: Recalculate stored build costs for every manufacturable item. Runs automatically after a market refresh; use this to force an update after changing pricing or overrides.

data.name: PurchaseAComponentInstead
data.value: Purchase a component instead of building when its market value is ≤

data.name: OffByDefaultComponentNote
data.value: Off by default. Component markets bounce around, and a few units listed cheap don't guarantee the quantity you need is available at that price — nor that it's worth tracking down and hauling. When off, the calculators build every component they can (items that genuinely can't be costed are still bought). Turn it on to let cheaper-of-build-vs-buy decide.

data.name: AdjustHowOftenEachNote
data.value: Adjust how often each endpoint is polled. Changes take effect on the next poll cycle.

data.name: TipResetTheInMemory
data.value: Reset the in-memory timer so this endpoint fires on the next poll cycle (within ~10 seconds).

data.name: WhenResolvingUnknownStructureNote
data.value: When resolving unknown structure names, EVE Console tries each authenticated character in turn until one succeeds. If most structures deny access to your characters, choosing a single character here prevents unnecessary failed calls and avoids burning your ESI error budget.

data.name: SelectNoneTryAllNote
data.value: Select '(none — try all)' to fall back to the original behaviour of trying every character. The choice takes effect immediately — no restart required.

data.name: ABackgroundServiceIsNote
data.value: A background service is installed while this client is on SQLite. Only one process may hold a SQLite file, so whichever starts first locks the other out. Stop and remove it, or switch this client to PostgreSQL.

data.name: ASmallSeparateProcessNote
data.value: A small separate process that shows which client is doing the background work, and opens the Background Processes window or a new EVE Console from its menu. It never does the background work itself, and it never handles alarms — closing EVE Console is how you stop those.

data.name: ReadsEvesOwnGameNote
data.value: Reads EVE's own game logs and stores what it finds — combat, mining, bounties, jumps, undocking — so other tools can query it. Logs are opened read-only; nothing is ever written back and nothing is sent to the game client.

data.name: ThisCapturesActivityFromNote
data.value: This captures activity from now on. Logs EVE has already written are only loaded if you run an import below.

data.name: ParsePositionIsRememberedNote
data.value: Parse position is remembered per file, so anything logged while EVE Console was closed is picked up the next time it starts.

data.name: LeaveTheListEmptyNote
data.value: Leave the list empty to use the local folder automatically. Add a network path (\\MACHINE\share\Gamelogs) to import logs from EVE clients running on other computers — nothing needs to be installed on them.

data.name: TurningTheImporterOnNote
data.value: Turning the importer on only picks up new activity from that point. To also load what EVE has already logged, choose how far back to go and start the import. This runs once — afterwards new activity is picked up automatically.

data.name: KeepLinesThatNoRule
data.value: Keep lines that no rule recognised

data.name: RecommendedEvesLogFormatNote
data.value: Recommended. EVE's log format is undocumented and varies by client version, and recognition rules can only cover activity someone has actually done. Keeping unrecognised lines (as kind 'unmatched') means missing coverage shows up in your own data instead of going unnoticed.

data.name: UnlikeGameLogsChatNote
data.value: Unlike game logs, chat logs contain what other people wrote. Nothing is stored unless you both enable this and tick specific channels below.

data.name: NotePrivateConversationsAppearNote
data.value: Note: private conversations appear as "Private Chat (2)", "Private Chat (3)" and so on. EVE reuses those names for different people over time, so ticking one can capture direct messages with many different players.

data.name: LeaveTheListEmptyNote2
data.value: Leave the list empty to use the local folder automatically. Add a network path (\\MACHINE\share\Chatlogs) to import logs from EVE clients running on other computers — nothing needs to be installed on them. Channel discovery below only sees channels from the folder(s) configured here.

data.name: OnlyTickedChannelsAreNote
data.value: Only ticked channels are read at all — files for other channels are never opened. Discovery reads filenames only; it can take a moment as these folders hold tens of thousands of files.

data.name: AsWithGameLogsNote
data.value: As with game logs, enabling only captures new messages. Use this to also load past chat for the selected channels.

data.name: JumpsKillsSovereigntyIndustryNote
data.value: Jumps, kills, sovereignty, industry indices, faction warfare and incursions, used by the Universe map overlays. ESI serves only the current hour, so history comes from the EVE Ref archive — which means closing the app does not leave permanent gaps.

data.name: PastTheHourlyWindowNote
data.value: Past the hourly window, jumps and kills are totalled per day, and sovereignty, industry and structure data keep one snapshot a day. Industry indices are still refreshed every hour, so the current value stays current — only the older hours are thinned.

data.name: EsiOnlyReturnsANote
data.value: ESI only returns a killmail when you were the victim or got the final blow — participating in a kill without the final blow is invisible to it. zKillboard tracks every participant, so merging it in fills that gap. On by default, for your own characters and their corporations; untick it to turn it off. Merges into the same Kills data used everywhere else, never duplicates or overwrites what ESI already provided.

data.name: LiveCapturePollsZkillboardNote
data.value: Live capture polls zKillboard for just the characters and corps already tracked in this app, at the interval below.

data.name: LiveCaptureSwitchesToNote
data.value: Live capture switches to zKillboard's real-time firehose, which has no interval to set — it streams continuously. Database size will grow substantially faster than Mine+Corp mode, since every kill in New Eden is stored, not just your own.

data.name: CheckZkillboardForNewNote
data.value: Check zKillboard for new kills every (s):

data.name: NotUsedInAllNote
data.value: Not used in All-kills scope — the firehose paces itself instead.

data.name: PullsZkillboardsDailyKillNote
data.value: Pulls zKillboard's daily kill dumps for the chosen range and merges in anything matching the scope above. Also runs automatically once an hour to catch up on any gap since the app was last running — this button is mainly for pulling in history from before tracking started.

data.name: SubmitsKillmailsThisAppNote
data.value: Submits killmails this app has that zKillboard is missing — typically ESI kills that nobody else uploaded. Only kills from the covered date range below are considered, and only once they are a few hours old, so a kill still working its way through zKillboard is never submitted needlessly. Nothing is ever submitted twice.

data.name: ThatIsTheOldestNote
data.value: That is the oldest kill confirmed present on zKillboard. Anything older predates everything zKillboard has shown us, so it can't be judged missing and is left alone — backfill further back to widen the range.

data.name: TheHeadingEachSectionNote
data.value: The heading each section is posted under. Leave one empty to use the built-in name. Every Top 10 heading carries the month it covers, so a list read on its own still says which month it is.

data.name: HintPutInFrontOf
data.value: Put in front of the summary's first line
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: AnyoneHereIsLeftNote
data.value: Anyone here is left out of every Top 10 list, on this tab and in scheduled posts.

data.name: HintTypeTwoLettersOfThe
data.value: Type two letters of the name…
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: EveryModelTheAgentNote
data.value: Every model the agent can think with: a server of your own such as Ollama, which is free, or a paid service. Which one does what is set under Roles below.

data.name: HintSkAnt
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: OneKeyForEveryNote
data.value: One key for every Claude model in the list.

data.name: GetYourAnthropicApi
data.value: Get your Anthropic API key at console.anthropic.com

data.name: HintSk
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: OneKeyForEveryNote2
data.value: One key for every OpenAI model in the list, and for OpenAI's voices and speech input.

data.name: GetYourOpenaiApi
data.value: Get your OpenAI API key at platform.openai.com

data.name: TipAskTheServiceFor
data.value: Ask the service for its list of models again

data.name: ForModelsThatThinkNote
data.value: For models that think before they answer, such as Qwen3. The thinking is never shown, but every answer waits for it. Untick for quicker replies: the model is told not to think, at some cost in care — most of all in choosing a tool. Models that do not think ignore it.

data.name: AnthropicKeepsTheInstructionsNote
data.value: Anthropic keeps the instructions, tools and conversation cached between messages, and reading the cache costs a tenth of sending it again. The entry lives 5 minutes from the last message; every message renews it. If your messages are usually 5–60 minutes apart, the 1-hour option saves money — but writing the cache then costs 2× instead of 1.25×, so it costs more if they are closer together. The AI Usage tool shows cache reads and writes per message. For every Claude model in the list.

data.name: TipAsksItForOne
data.value: Asks it for one sentence, as set here, before saving. Free on a server of your own; a few tokens on a paid service.

data.name: TalksWithYouAndNote
data.value: Talks with you and works the app — opens and arranges its tools, sets alarms and destinations, remembers your standing instructions.

data.name: IfItStopsAnsweringNote
data.value: If it stops answering, fall over to

data.name: SaySoWhenIt
data.value: Say so when it falls over, and when it comes back — in the chat, and aloud when speaking

data.name: AnythingThatNeedsYourNote
data.value: Anything that needs your database or ESI — what you have, own, are doing or have done. The model here gets the whole prompt and every tool.

data.name: SendAMessageToNote
data.value: Send a message to this model when…

data.name: CompactsOlderMessagesWhenNote
data.value: Compacts older messages when the conversation grows long (see Context Management). A small free model does this well.

data.name: SaidForARoleNote
data.value: Said for a role that says so (above) when its model stops answering and the fallback takes over, and again when its own model is back. {user} is your name from Personalisation, {purpose} is "our conversation" or "data access", {primary} and {fallback} are the two models' names. Nothing is switched silently at start: if a role's own model is not there, the first message finds out, and says so.

data.name: MinutesBetweenOneChangeNote
data.value: minutes between one change and the next switch back

data.name: MinutesWithoutABreakNote
data.value: minutes without a break before a role's own model returns

data.name: AModelThatStopsNote
data.value: A model that stops answering is replaced at once, before a word of the answer — these only govern coming back, so a server that keeps dropping out cannot make the agent flip back and forth. A switch back waits for your next message, and for one real word from the returning model.

data.name: EverythingOnThisTabNote
data.value: Everything on this tab is about you rather than this PC, so it is kept in the database and shared by every client that opens it. The other tabs — provider, keys, voice, microphone — are this machine's own.

data.name: ConciseShortDirectAnswersNote
data.value: Concise: short, direct answers (1-3 sentences). Balanced: complete but not padded. Detailed: thorough with context and reasoning. This is injected into the system prompt every time you send a message.

data.name: InOrderOfPreferenceNote
data.value: In order of preference. The first voice that can speak is used; if it fails, the next takes over at once and, when the first is back and has stayed up, it returns. A voice can have a name of its own — the voice is part of who you are talking to — and while it speaks it is the agent's name, in the panel and in the conversation. A voice with no name goes by the agent's name from Personalisation.

data.name: TipPreferThisVoiceOver
data.value: Prefer this voice over the one above it

data.name: Kokoro82mRunsFullyNote
data.value: Kokoro 82M runs fully offline on this PC. Its voices ship with the application; its model is downloaded once.

data.name: OneModelServesEveryNote
data.value: One model serves every Kokoro voice. It is downloaded once (~320 MB, only the neural network weights — no executable code) into this PC's data folder, where updates leave it alone.

data.name: AnyServerThatSpeaksNote
data.value: Any server that speaks OpenAI's speech API — Kokoro-FastAPI, Chatterbox-TTS-Server (full or Turbo), Orpheus-FastAPI — usually on another machine's GPU. Free to use; if the server cannot speak, the next voice in the list takes over.

data.name: HintAsTheServerNames
data.value: as the server names it — kokoro, chatterbox, orpheus…
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: HintAsTheServerNames2
data.value: as the server names it — af_heart, tara…
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: ChatterboxAFileFromNote
data.value: Chatterbox: a file from its voices folder, with .wav — Emily.wav (it ignores the model). Orpheus: tara, leah, jess, leo, dan, mia, zac or zoe (model orpheus). Kokoro-FastAPI: af_heart, bf_emma… (model kokoro).

data.name: ApiKeyOnlyIfNote
data.value: API key (only if the server asks for one)

data.name: PiperIsAFastNote
data.value: Piper is a fast offline engine. Its runtime ships with the application; only the voice model is downloaded.

data.name: OneKeyForEveryNote3
data.value: One key for every OpenAI voice, and for the Agent tab's OpenAI models and speech input.

data.name: HintAsOpenaiNamesIt
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: TipAskOpenaiForIts
data.value: Ask OpenAI for its list of speech models again

data.name: OneKeyForEveryElevenlabs
data.value: One key for every ElevenLabs voice.

data.name: GetYourElevenlabsApi
data.value: Get your ElevenLabs API key at elevenlabs.io

data.name: HintTheVoicesId
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: TipAskElevenlabsForYour
data.value: Ask ElevenLabs for your voices again — after adding one there, say

data.name: HintTheModelsId
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: TipAskElevenlabsForIts
data.value: Ask ElevenLabs for its list of models again

data.name: TipSpeaksWithThisVoice
data.value: Speaks with this voice as set here, before saving — on its own, not through the list

data.name: AnnounceItInTheNew
data.value: Announce it, in the new voice

data.name: SaidByTheVoiceNote
data.value: Said by the voice taking over, and kept in the conversation so the agent knows who it is now. Only when the name changes — give each voice its own name for a change to be announced. Nothing is said when the app starts: you simply hear whoever is speaking. {previous} and {current} stand for the two names.

data.name: MinutesWithoutABreakNote2
data.value: minutes without a break before a preferred voice returns

data.name: AVoiceThatFailsNote
data.value: A voice that fails is replaced at once — these only govern coming back, so a server that keeps dropping out cannot make the voice flip back and forth. A switch back waits for the end of the current answer.

data.name: HintSystemDefault
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: TipRefreshTheListOfInput
data.value: Refresh the list of input devices

data.name: SystemDefaultFollowsWhateverNote
data.value: System default follows whatever the operating system has as its input device, so a headset plugged in later is used without coming back here. Pick a device to pin it. Works on both Windows and Linux (PortAudio); if the list is empty, click ↺ to refresh after your audio driver initialises.

data.name: TheSameOpenaiKeyNote
data.value: The same OpenAI key as the Agent tab's OpenAI models and OpenAI's voices.

data.name: TipAskOpenaiForIts2
data.value: Ask OpenAI for its list of transcription models again

data.name: SentToOpenaiToNote
data.value: Sent to OpenAI to be written down. Works on Windows and Linux.

data.name: RunsWhisperNetLocallyNote
data.value: Runs Whisper.net locally on this machine (Windows only). No API key required. A model file must be downloaded before first use.

data.name: HintEn
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: ATwoLetterCodeNote
data.value: A two-letter code such as en, or auto to let the model guess. A guess on a two-second clip is often wrong, and it costs an extra pass; name the language you speak.

data.name: PostFromEveConsoleNote
data.value: Post from EVE Console straight into Slack. Posts are made with your own user token, so they appear as you — not as a bot. Nothing is posted automatically; you choose when to send.

data.name: ConnectingOpensSlackInNote
data.value: Connecting opens Slack in your browser. Choose the workspace, approve access, and you're done — EVE Console never sees your Slack password, and you can revoke it any time from your Slack account settings.

data.name: N1OpenApiSlackNote
data.value: 1. Open api.slack.com/apps and choose Create New App → From scratch. Name it (e.g. EVE Console) and pick your workspace.

data.name: N2GoToOauthNote
data.value: 2. Go to OAuth & Permissions and add these under User Token Scopes (not Bot Token Scopes):

data.name: N3ClickInstallToNote
data.value: 3. Click Install to Workspace and approve, then copy the User OAuth Token (it starts with xoxp-).

data.name: HintXoxp
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: StoredLocallyInYourNote
data.value: Stored locally in your EVE Console database. Treat it like a password — it can post as you in any channel you can reach.

data.name: ForWorkspacesYouCannotNote
data.value: For workspaces you cannot connect to as yourself — an alliance Slack, typically, which will hand out a webhook where it would never hand out a token. Name one here and it appears in every destination list below.

data.name: AWebhookCannotThreadNote
data.value: ⚠ A webhook cannot thread. Nothing posted through one returns a message id, so a sale posting's detail arrives as a second message instead of a reply under the first. Posts also arrive as the webhook's own app rather than as you.

data.name: HintName
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: PickWhichChannelEachNote
data.value: Pick which channel each part of EVE Console posts to. A section's post button only appears once its channel is set.

data.name: HintSelectAChannel
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in SettingsWindow.

data.name: PrivateChannelsOnlyAppearNote
data.value: Private channels only appear if you are a member of them. If a channel is missing, use Reload Channels.

data.name: ConfigureWhichConditionsTriggerNote
data.value: Configure which conditions trigger alerts on the Overview tab. Alerts are re-evaluated each time the Overview is refreshed.

data.name: CharacterSkillQueueIs
data.value: Character skill queue is paused (has entries but nothing training)

data.name: SkillQueueWillBeEmpty
data.value: Skill queue will be empty within

data.name: AlertWhenItemsAre
data.value: Alert when items are moved into Asset Safety

data.name: TriggersWhenAStructureitemsmovedintosafetyNote
data.value: Triggers when a StructureItemsMovedIntoSafety notification is received for any authenticated character. The alert persists until you manually dismiss it.

data.name: AlertWhenStandingProjects
data.value: Alert when standing projects are not currently active

data.name: TriggersWhenOneOrNote
data.value: Triggers when one or more standing projects (Corp Activity → Projects → Standing Projects) have no matching active ESI corp project. Re-evaluated each time the Overview refreshes.

data.name: AlertWhenStandingBuy
data.value: Alert when standing buy orders need attention

data.name: TriggersWhenAStandingNote
data.value: Triggers when a standing buy order (Market / Trade → Standing Buy Orders) has no matching live order, has been outbid at that station, has fallen below 10% of its original volume, or has under 20% of its duration left. The alert says which, since placing an order, raising a price, topping one up and renewing one are different jobs. Re-evaluated each time the Overview refreshes.

data.name: OutbidDetectionComparesAgainstNote
data.value: Outbid detection compares against the public order book, which only covers stations and structures configured as market sources under Settings → Market. Anywhere else shows a dash rather than claiming there is no competition.

data.name: AlertWhenRunningJobs
data.value: Alert when running jobs are in a facility not rigged for them

data.name: CountsActiveManufacturingAndNote
data.value: Counts active manufacturing and reaction jobs whose facility has no rig bonusing that kind of work. Research, copying and invention are not counted — they use rigs this check does not model.

data.name: OnlyFacilitiesLinkedToNote
data.value: Only facilities linked to an Indy Parks structure can be judged: ESI cannot report what rigs a structure has fitted, so the rigs are whatever you described in Indy Parks. Link a structure to a real facility there to include it. Unlinked facilities are ignored rather than reported as unrigged.

data.name: AlertWhenIndustryJobs
data.value: Alert when industry jobs are ready to deliver

data.name: CountsJobsPastTheirNote
data.value: Counts jobs past their end date, or marked ready, that nobody has delivered yet — the output is waiting and the slot is held until someone collects it. Covers every character and corporation the app polls jobs for; jobs are polled every 15 minutes by default (Timers), so a job that just finished may take that long to show.

data.name: AlertAboutOutstandingContracts
data.value: Alert about outstanding contracts issued to you

data.name: CountsActiveContractsAssignedNote
data.value: Counts active contracts assigned to one of your characters or personal corporations — the ones waiting on you. The alert opens the Contracts tool on them, soonest to expire first.

data.name: AlertAboutContractsAboutTo
data.value: Alert about contracts about to expire

data.name: CountsActiveContractsYouNote
data.value: Counts active contracts you issued, or that are assigned to you, that are in the last 15% of their life: a two-week contract from its twelfth day. Personal corporations count as you.

data.name: ThisIsNotTheNote
data.value: This is not the database currently open. Save the choice and restart EVE Console for it to take effect.

data.name: PostgresPostgresqlAndTheNote
data.value: Postgres, PostgreSQL and the Slonik Logo are trademarks or registered trademarks of the PostgreSQL Community Association of Canada, and used with their permission.

data.name: EveConsoleNeedsToNote
data.value: EVE Console needs to connect to this database and create tables in it. The simplest arrangement is a database owned by this user — CREATE DATABASE eveconsole OWNER myuser — which grants what is needed without any further permissions.

data.name: ReplaceWhatIsOnThe
data.value: Replace what is on the server

data.name: MovingShrinkingAndBackingNote
data.value: Moving, shrinking and backing up act on the database FILE, so they apply to SQLite only. A PostgreSQL server is backed up with its own tools.

data.name: TipMoveTheDatabaseTo
data.value: Move the database to another folder or drive, or give it a different name. The application restarts to do it.

data.name: TipRebuildTheDatabaseFile
data.value: Rebuild the database file so space freed by deleted data is returned to your drive. Restarts the application.

data.name: TheseOperationsCopyOrNote
data.value: These operations copy or move the database file and restart the application.

data.name: AServersDatabaseCannotNote
data.value: A server's database cannot be backed up by copying a file — the file belongs to the server and may not even be on this machine — so EVE Console runs pg_dump, which asks the server for a consistent snapshot. Dumps are written in the custom format, which is compressed and can be restored whole or table by table with pg_restore.

data.name: ReplacesEverythingInTheNote
data.value: Replaces everything in the database with the contents of a .dump file. Anything polled since that backup was taken is lost. EVE Console restarts to do it, because the restore drops every table and cannot run while the app is holding them.

data.name: WhatTheDatabaseIsNote
data.value: What the database is spent on, table data and indexes separately. On SQLite the figures are measured from the data and scaled to the file's used pages, with large tables sampled rather than read in full. On PostgreSQL the sizes are exact and the row counts are the server's estimates. Either way it is for deciding what is worth keeping, not a byte-level audit.

data.name: HowLongEveConsoleNote
data.value: How long EVE Console keeps data it can afford to forget. Every rule here is off until you turn it on, and each runs once at startup. Purging removes rows, but SQLite reuses the freed pages rather than returning them, so the file itself only gets smaller after a compaction — see Database → Shrink Database. Database → Storage Breakdown shows where the space actually went.

data.name: TheErrorLogIsNote
data.value: The error log is for reading the last few hours, not for keeping history. Left unattended it grows past a hundred thousand entries, at which point nobody looks at it. Under 1% of a measured 4 GB database, so this keeps the log readable rather than reclaiming space.

data.name: RemovesTheKillAndNote
data.value: Removes the kill and everything attached to it — attackers, items, references and zKillboard flags. Kill mails and their indexes are the largest thing in a typical database (61% of a measured 4 GB file), so this is the rule that actually reclaims space. ⚠️ Deleted kills are gone locally; getting them back means re-fetching from ESI or zKillboard, and ESI only serves recent ones.

data.name: RemovesDailyMarketHistoryNote
data.value: Removes daily market history per region and type, together with the derived per-type price snapshots built from it — both together, because keeping one without the other leaves a history that disagrees with itself. About 15% of a measured 4 GB file. ESI serves roughly a year of history, so recent rows can be re-fetched.

data.name: RemovesParsedGameLogNote
data.value: Removes parsed game-log events — ratting, mining and industry activity read from your EVE client logs. The .log files on disk are left alone, so anything purged here can be re-imported with Game Logs → Import Past Logs for as long as those files survive.

data.name: PurgeGameLogEventsOlder
data.value: Purge game log events older than

data.name: RemovesStoredChatMessagesNote
data.value: Removes stored chat messages. Intel reports already parsed from them are kept — reports older than the oldest surviving message are treated as history that cannot be rebuilt, both by the startup cleanup and by Chat Logs → parse stored history, which rebuilds only the period it can actually reproduce. The .log files on disk are untouched, so a re-import stays possible while they exist.

data.name: RemovesTheRecordOfNote
data.value: Removes the record of past AI Agent exchanges — what each one asked for, which tools it used, and the tokens it consumed. This is what the usage and cost figures are calculated from, so purging it shortens the history those can cover. It is the app's own diagnostic record rather than your data, so unlike the sections above this one is on by default; untick it to keep everything.

data.name: ChecksOnStartupAndNote
data.value: Checks on startup and once an hour. When a new version is found you'll be prompted; declining won't ask again until the next version.
